info.name: Restful-Booker API Tests
info.description:
Comprehensive API test collection for the Restful-Booker practice API (https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com).

Targets: Health, Authentication, Booking CRUD, Negative cases, and Security edge cases.
Author: Aniruddha Yadav | QA Engineer
Collection Version: 1.0.0
API Docs: https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/apidoc/index.html

item.name: 00 Health
item.description: Verifies the API is reachable. GET /ping should return 201 Created (docs: Health Check endpoint).

request.description: Checks the API is alive. Expected: 201 Created (per docs: 'Returns a 201 to let you know everything is in order').

exec: // Docs state: 'Returns a 201 to let you know everything is in order'
pm.test('Status code is 201 Created (docs: Ping endpoint)', function () {

item.name: 01 Authentication
item.description:
Tests the POST /auth endpoint with valid credentials, wrong password, empty body, and missing fields.
A successful auth saves {{token}} to environment for use in subsequent requests.

request.description: Authenticates with admin/password123 (public practice credentials). Saves the token to environment.

exec: // Docs state: '200 OK' with { token: string }
pm.test('Status code is 200 OK (docs: Auth CreateToken)', function () {
pm.test('Token is a non-empty string', function () {
// Save token to environment for subsequent requests

request.description: Negative: wrong password. API returns 200 with { reason: 'Bad credentials' } instead of a 4xx (non-standard REST behavior).

exec: // NOTE: Restful-Booker returns 200 OK even for bad credentials,
// with body { 'reason': 'Bad credentials' } instead of a 401.
// This is a deliberate non-standard behaviour of this practice API.
pm.test('Status code is 200 (API returns 200 for bad creds — non-standard behaviour)', function () {
pm.test('Response body contains error reason (no token issued)', function () {
// Must NOT contain a valid token
pm.test('No sensitive data (password) leaked in error response', function () {

request.description: Negative: empty JSON body. No credentials provided.

exec: // Restful-Booker does not strictly validate empty body at auth endpoint.
// It returns 200 with { reason: 'Bad credentials' } for missing credentials.
pm.test('Status code is 200 (API does not return 4xx for empty auth body)', function () {
pm.test('Response body contains reason field (no token for empty body)', function () {
pm.test('No token issued for empty body', function () {
pm.test('No sensitive data leaked in response', function () {

request.description: Negative: username field missing from the body.

exec: // API returns 200 with { reason: 'Bad credentials' } for missing username.
pm.test('Status code is 200 (missing username treated as bad credentials)', function () {
pm.test('No token issued for missing username', function () {
pm.test('Error is handled gracefully (no stack trace or server error in body)', function () {

request.description: Negative: firstname field missing. The API's actual behaviour is observed here.

exec: // NOTE: Restful-Booker does NOT always validate required fields strictly.
// The ideal REST response would be 400 Bad Request, but this API
// may return 200 or 500 depending on its internal validation.
// We assert: either a 4xx error OR a 200 with the field blank/null.
pm.test('Response indicates missing field is handled (not a 5xx server crash)', function () {
pm.test('No sensitive internal error details leaked', function () {

request.description: Negative: all fields have wrong data types. Verifies the API handles type mismatches gracefully.

exec: // NOTE: Restful-Booker may accept wrong types silently (coerce them)
// or return a 400/500. The ideal REST behavior is 400.
// We verify the API does not crash and no internal errors are exposed.
pm.test('API does not return an unhandled 5xx for wrong types', function () {
pm.test('No stack trace or exception details leaked', function () {

request.description: Negative: completely empty JSON body. Expects a 4xx or handled response.

exec: // Empty body should be rejected. API may return 400 or 200 depending on validation.
pm.test('Empty body does not cause an unhandled 5xx crash', function () {
pm.test('Error handled gracefully (no internal details exposed)', function () {

item.name: 06 Negative and Security
item.description: Negative and security edge-case tests: unauthenticated updates/deletes, invalid tokens, unsupported headers, long strings, and special characters.

request.description: Security: PUT without any auth header/cookie. Expect 403 Forbidden.

exec: // Docs state: 403 Forbidden when not authorised
// NOTE: We use bookingId=1 (a pre-existing public booking) to avoid
// modifying data we created, while still testing the auth gate.
pm.test('Status code is 403 Forbidden (no auth — docs: UpdateBooking)', function () {
pm.test('No sensitive data in 403 response', function () {

request.description: Security: PUT with an invalid (fake) token. Expect 403.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 403 Forbidden (invalid token)', function () {
pm.test('No sensitive data leaked in invalid token response', function () {

request.description: Security: DELETE without any auth. Should be rejected with 403. Uses bookingId=1 (pre-existing public booking — we do NOT own it, so we depend on the auth gate to stop the operation).

exec: // If the API is working correctly, this MUST return 403.
// If it returns 201, that is a defect — unauthenticated delete was allowed.
pm.test('Status code is 403 Forbidden (no auth DELETE)', function () {

request.description: Security: DELETE with an obviously invalid token. Should be rejected with 403.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 403 Forbidden (invalid token DELETE)', function () {

request.description: Security: PATCH without auth. Should return 403.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 403 Forbidden (no auth PATCH)', function () {

request.description: Edge case: requesting XML format via Accept header. The API may return JSON anyway or a 406.

exec: // REST best practice: 406 Not Acceptable for unsupported Accept header.

pm.test('API responds (200 or 406 — both acceptable; 5xx is not)', function () {
pm.test('No server crash on unsupported Accept header', function () {
